title: Omni Documents are the Artifact's explicit escape hatch for activity the primitive taxonomy does not cover
content:
A.6.1.1.4.3 opens a second top-level branch of the Skybase Artifact alongside Sky Primitives: "The documents herein define Skybase's strategic intent and operational processes relating to infrastructure inherited from Sky Core, activities unrelated to Sky Primitives, or activities spanning multiple Sky Primitives."

The three cases it names are precisely the ones a primitive-indexed structure cannot hold. Inherited infrastructure belongs to no Invocation. Activity unrelated to any primitive has no Instance to live in. And activity spanning several primitives would have to be duplicated across them or arbitrarily assigned to one.

What lands here proves the need. Skybase's *strategies* for the Distribution Reward, Integration Boost and Core Governance Reward primitives sit in Omni Documents (A.6.1.1.4.3.2), not inside those primitives — because strategy governs which Instances to invoke, and so cannot be the property of any single Instance. The USDS Demand Subsidies programme (A.6.1.1.4.3.4) sits here because it is direct capital deployment with no primitive at all. Forum and Discord venues, the Ecosystem Accord 7 commitment, and the emergency response protocols sit here for the same reason.

The design lesson is that a rigid classification scheme needs a declared remainder, or material gets forced into the nearest ill-fitting slot and becomes unfindable. Naming the remainder — and stating the three conditions for using it — keeps the primitive tree honest: an Instance directory contains only Instances.

The risk is the mirror image: an unbounded Omni branch can absorb anything, and material placed there escapes the per-primitive uniformity that makes the rest of the Artifact machine-readable.
description: They hold strategic intent, infrastructure inherited from Sky Core, activity unrelated to any Sky Primitive, and activity spanning several of them.
